Integrated Growth & PR · She Got Buckets (SGB) · Feb – Apr 2026
Mind Over Hoops: Integrated PR & Growth Campaign
Scaling a Sports × Mental Health Tournament Through Earned Media & Institutional Partnerships — Zero Paid Budget

Campaign Context

She Got Buckets (SGB), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit empowering Asian women through basketball, was preparing for its national finals in Howard County, Maryland — returning to the region for the third consecutive year. The 2026 edition introduced a new strategic dimension: Mind Over Hoops, an initiative connecting athletic participation to mental resilience, identity development, and emotional well-being.

The challenge: build regional legitimacy, earn institutional credibility, and drive tournament awareness — entirely through earned media and strategic partnerships, with no paid advertising budget.

Objectives

  • Secure minimum 5 media mentions and 1 regional sports feature before April 3
  • Establish Howard Community College (HCC) as an official institutional partner
  • Reposition the tournament from a standalone event to a sports × mental health movement
  • Build a scalable PR infrastructure replicable for future tournaments
  • Drive Instagram reach of 10K+ and LinkedIn engagement rate of 6%+

Strategy

Leverage institutional authority + earned media sequencing + narrative repositioning to create exponential credibility lift — without paid acquisition.

01
Institutional Anchoring
Partner with Howard Community College to unlock official website features, newsletter placement, podcast access, and executive visibility
02
Earned Media Flywheel
Press Conference → Press Release → Newsletter → Podcast (Inside the Dragon's Lair) → Radio → PR Newswire → Regional Sports Outlets
03
Narrative Repositioning
"Basketball tournament" → "Sports × Mental Health Movement." Athlete stories anchor authenticity; wellness center partnerships anchor credibility
04
Countdown Amplification
7–10 day organic social push: player quote cards, founder video, countdown graphics across Instagram, LinkedIn, and Threads

  • Drafted long-form press release distributed via PR Newswire and SGB website
  • Coordinated press conference on Feb 20 with HCC, local officials, and SGB leadership — featuring remarks on Mind Over Hoops initiative
  • Prepared media pitch deck (600–800 word version) targeting ESPN Regional, Baltimore Sun, and Washington Post Local Sports
  • Built unified media timeline and distribution schedule for PR team

  • PR Activation #1 — HCC Website & Social: Coordinated joint player interview on mental strength and identity in sports; distributed via HCC website, Instagram, and LinkedIn

  • PR Activation #3 — Radio Interview: Coordinated radio appearance covering mental health in women's sports, SGB mission, and April 3 call-to-action
  • PR Activation #4 — Podcast: Secured guest spot on HCC's Inside the Dragon's Lair athletics podcast, invited by Dragon Podcast Manager Ryan Record

  • Virtual panel: Mental Health in Competitive Sports — featuring mental health professional, HCC athlete, SGB athlete, and SGB founder
  • Content deliverables: 1 full panel recording, 3 short-form Reels, 1 LinkedIn long-form post, joint HCC × SGB social post
  • Partnership with Maryland mental health organization to anchor institutional legitimacy

Campaign Context

The 5th China International Import Expo (CIIE) is the world's first import-themed national expo. Intel participated November 5–10, 2022 in Shanghai with a 200-square-meter exhibition booth themed "Moving Toward a Digital Future" — showcasing a metaverse basketball experience, digital transformation solutions, and green sustainable technology.

Two flagship events anchored the campaign on Nov 6: a sub-forum on digital talent cultivation (part of the Hongqiao International Economic Forum) and a Metaverse Sports Solution launch co-presented with the Chinese Basketball Association (CBA). Senior Intel executives delivered keynotes alongside representatives from UNESCO, UNDP, and Chinese government agencies.

Data Analytics & Content Strategy · USC CMGT 564 Final Project · May 2025
XYZ+ Strategic Activation & Programming Recommendations
Genre-Level ROI Analysis · IP Acquisition Framework · Targeted Audience Activation — Built on Big Data

Project Overview

XYZ+ is a fictional streaming platform (modeled on the scale of Disney+) seeking to optimize its content investment and subscriber growth strategy. As part of a 5-person consulting team at USC, we acted as the Data & Analytics Department — advising on programming decisions, IP licensing priorities, and targeted marketing activation using audience behavioral data.

The project spanned four analytical pillars: Big Data & forecasting infrastructure, Programming Strategy (genre-type performance), IP Investment (franchise acquisition recommendations), and Targeted Activation (comedy audience segmentation and A/B testing).

My Focus Areas Programming Strategy (genre analysis & content mix recommendations) + IP Investment (franchise evaluation & acquisition recommendations)

My Contribution

01 Programming Strategy
  • Analyzed XYZ+'s existing content library across 9 genre-type combinations (series vs. movie × genre)
  • Computed Cost Per View (CPV) and Cost Per Subscriber (CPS) efficiency metrics for each genre
  • Built a cost-effectiveness scatter plot revealing that Reality, Drama & Action Series lead on both CPV and CPS efficiency
  • Identified that Series drives 89% of total streams and 80% of subscriber acquisition despite only 50% of budget allocation
  • Recommended rebalancing toward Drama/Reality for efficiency, and Kids/Comedy for acquisition volume
02 IP Investment & Franchise Analysis
  • Evaluated 7 Lionsgate IP franchises using a multi-dimensional framework: Google Search trends, box office ROI, franchise scalability, and social audience size
  • Cross-referenced 12-month Google Trends data for all candidates to assess sustained cultural relevance
  • Analyzed Twilight ($3.31B total gross), Now You See Me ($686M across 2 films), and The Rookie (43% streaming viewership, 70% of 18–49s via SVOD)
  • Delivered final acquisition recommendation: Twilight + Now You See Me + The Rookie — balancing franchise depth, cross-gen fanbase, and streaming-native audience migration

Evaluation Framework Applied
Search & Social: Google Trends + social media data (12-month window)
Commercial ROI: Historical box office vs. production budget
Franchise Potential: Reboot, spin-off, or extended universe viability
Streaming Fit: SVOD audience migration potential and digital-native demographics

What I Coded
  • Built the Weibo crawler from scratch — scrapes posts ranked by engagement across 400 entries/day
  • Designed the reweighted scoring formula: 70% comments + 30% views, with log normalization and daily aggregation of top 100 topics
  • Integrated OpenAI GPT API replacing legacy dictionary-based models — unlocked detection of nuanced emotion including sarcasm and political distrust
  • Built the shadow ban detection algorithm: identified statistically implausible data patterns indicating platform content suppression
  • Automated visualization pipeline: donut charts, word clouds, and bilingual topic cards generated per report cycle
  • Architecting next phase: multi-agent AI system where separate agents handle scraping, analysis, visualization, and report drafting autonomously
View on GitHub

Product 1 — Weekly Trending Topics

The crawler ranks 2,800 posts/week through a multi-step scoring formula, then curates the top 15 topics into three bilingual category reports delivered to USCI diplomacy researchers.

Product 2 — Dual-Layer Sentiment Analysis

Each topic runs through two parallel GPT analyses: a 5-class sentiment score (left) and a multi-label emotion breakdown (right). Together they give a complete picture of how Chinese netizens respond to a given news event.

Layer 1 — 5-class sentiment scoring: #纪念台湾光复# (Taiwan Retrocession anniversary)
Layer 2 — Multi-label emotion tagging: #蔡国强烟花秀调查# (Cai Guoqiang fireworks investigation)
Original — Chinese Weibo comments
English translation — dominant discourse terms from #纪念台湾光复# comments
Read Sample Report — "The Return of Taiwan Restoration Day"

Product 3 — Censorship & Shadow Ban Detection

The crawler surfaced statistically impossible data patterns, providing rare empirical evidence of how Weibo algorithmically controls information visibility.

88
topics with exactly 18 reads and 0 discussions — statistically implausible organic data
10
topics with fewer than 50 reads but over 1,000,000 discussions — engagement suppressed at display layer
4 Platform Suppression Mechanisms Identified
① Normal display
② Consolidation — emotional titles merged into neutral ones
③ Demotion — real engagement numbers hidden
④ Deletion / outright blocking
Current Impact: Offers a rare empirical window into Chinese platform censorship — directly relevant to diplomatic and academic audiences studying Chinese public opinion formation.
Next Phase: Write long-form analytical articles on censorship patterns — pairing platform suppression data with real news events to surface how Weibo shapes political discourse and public memory.
